thread:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up re: service boundary refactor + tech-debt sweep. TL;DR — propose extracting config/telemetry/rollout logic out of runtime service into a smaller control-plane service so the runtime can be ultra-stable. Want a 3-month stability promise for public runtime API. Thoughts?

morgan: +1 on stability promise, but we need to pin what 'public runtime API' means. Are we freezing the REST surface or the internal protobufs too? :thinking:

anya: REST/gRPC surface for customers is what we freeze. Internal protobufs can evolve behind a compatibility shim, but we should avoid breaking customer-facing fields.

devon: Compatibility shim sounds right. Suggest we implement an adapter layer: runtime still implements v1, new control-plane talks v2 -> adapter translates. Keeps rollout simple.

oliver: Concern: moving telemetry out could change timing of metrics and increase cold-start noise. We'll need warmup + a migration plan for KV cache ownership.

jun: I can own contract tests between runtime and control-plane. We should add an automated suite that runs on every PR and a nightly integration run.

anya: Good. Proposed migration steps: 1) define control-plane API (write RFC follow-up doc) 2) add adapter in runtime (compat shim) 3) start canary with traffic routing flag 4) run contract tests & perf baseline 5) full cutover after 2 weeks stable.

morgan: For DB migrations: any schema changes must be backwards compatible. If we have to add columns, do phase deploys (read/write both formats). If we need a new table, create and backfill with streaming jobs.

devon: Also recommend feature flagging per-customer so we can route a subset to the new control-plane during the canary. Keeps blast radius small.

oliver: On perf: we'll gate canary based on 95th percentile latency and error budget burn. If latency delta > 5% or SLO breach, rollback. Also add a telemetry metric for 'control_plane_hop_count' to detect unexpected extra hops.

jun: Contract test checklist (draft):
- request/response shape validation
- error semantics (400/429/500 mapping)
- retry idempotency and dedupe keys
- streaming chunk boundaries
- kv cache headers retained
I'll PR the harness by EOD Monday.

anya: Nice. Ops/infra asks: who will be oncall during canary? We should notify eng-oncall and have a rollback runbook. @sre-bot can we schedule a pager window?

sre-bot: scheduled oncall window for canary 2026-03-25 09:00–17:00 UTC. Pager rotations: infra-team oncall.

morgan: Action items:
- anya: write RFC follow-up doc + API draft (due Thu)
- morgan: migration plan + DB backfill strategy (due Fri)
- devon: compatibility shim prototype (due next Wed)
- jun: contract test harness (EOD Mon)
- oliver: perf gating config + dashboard (due next Tue)

anya: I'm going to create the RFC follow-up doc and link it here. Quick note: try to keep surface area minimal — move only control/telemetry/rollout stuff out. Everything inference-path-critical stays in runtime. :thumbsup:

morgan: Sounds good. If nobody objects I'll kick off the follow-up doc and schedule a short design review this Friday. :calendar:
